title: V2: Federated OIDC/PKCE + owned authorization (shadow + short JWTs)
description:
Mission: Move from credential IdP (v1: email+argon2 + Loginer + long shadow cookie) to federated OIDC/PKCE IdP broker + local-owned authz (roles/function grants + shadow for revocation + short access JWTs for identity). Local creds + protosource-authmgr recover-admin stay as break-glass only. /authz/check and downstream authorizers remain the function grant gate.

All changes additive; v1 fully preserved. See V2_FEDERATION.md for the full design rationale, aggregate changes (LinkedIdentity on User, OIDCConfig on Issuer KIND_EXTERNAL), PKCE flows, and open design decisions.
design:
Core invariants (must hold):
- Additive only. Existing /login (creds), shadow cookie (default name configurable), Token.Issue path, bootstrap, mgr CLI recover-admin, Role grants, function matcher, all continue to work unchanged.
- Commit OIDC endpoint shapes now (in discovery doc + router) even if handlers stub/404 initially.
- Reuse heavily: Role grants unchanged, Token aggregate (new creation path), Key/Resolver (VerificationKey + JWKS already), Issuer KIND_EXTERNAL (extend), functions matcher, signers, keyproviders (also for client_secret).
- Sensitive material (client_secret on external issuers) encrypted via KeyProvider before persisting (same as signing keys). Plaintext only in process memory.
- Stateless where possible (signed cookies for PKCE state+verifier using our KIND_SELF keys, short TTL).
- Per-IdP JIT policy (default REJECT). 1 User : N linked identities (keyed '{issuer_id}:{subject}'), not 1:1.
- Break-glass local creds only for bootstrap/recover-admin.

Open design calls (settle before heavy coding, see V2_FEDERATION.md):
- N linked ids vs other models.
- Per-IdP JIT (REJECT default recommended).
- Break-glass local creds only.
- Full OIDC provider (not just broker).
- Exact path shapes (/oauth/*).
- Short access JWT claims (aud/scope/azp differences from shadow Token.jwt).
- Where to persist (or not) access JWTs vs ephemeral.
- Claim mapping defaults.
- /oauth/token for direct code exchange vs redirect-only for now.
- State cookie name/details.

Risks noted: Proto evolution on live stores (additive safe), secret handling (never in events/logs/responses), JIT races (deterministic user id or ErrAlreadyCreated tolerance), IdP clock skew (cache metadata/JWKS), cookie domain for oauth flows, HTTPS requirements.
acceptance_criteria: All v2 slices delivered additive-only. v1 paths (/login creds, default shadow cookie, Token.Issue, bootstrap, mgr recover-admin, Role grants, /authz/check, function matcher) continue to work unchanged for break-glass and existing consumers. Federated PKCE happy path works end-to-end with at least one external IdP (Google/Entra or test), producing linked User + shadow cookie + optional short access JWT. Discovery + JWKS + OIDCConfig configurator exercised. Full test -race green; manual verification per gates in epic notes. Docs updated to position local creds as break-glass. Mgr and frontend support for EXTERNAL OIDC issuers complete.
notes:
Current state snapshot (as of plan migration):
- Prep complete: dep bump to protosource v0.6.1, configurable shadow cookie name (PROTOSOURCE_AUTH_SHADOW_COOKIE_NAME), discovery doc stub + OIDC-shaped paths committed (/.well-known/openid-configuration + /oauth/* stubs), real JWKS endpoint (/oauth/jwks) with resolver extensions (VerifyUntil, SupportedAlgorithms, WithClock for tests).
- Phase 1 core complete: Issuer OIDCConfig proto (client_id, wrapped_client_secret + key_provider/master_key_ref, discovery_url or endpoints, allowed_audiences, claim_map, OIDCJITPolicy + jit_*), embedded on Issuer, Register extended, new SetOIDCConfig/ClearOIDCConfig cmds/events. Hand-written service/oidcconfig.go (NewOIDCConfigurator, Set/Clear/DecryptClientSecret/PrepareForRegister reusing KeyProvider exactly like keys/resolver). Roundtrip tests. Minimal frontend in IssuerDetail.tsx (client ID, configured badge, endpoints, JIT policy — never echoes secret). Temporary generator bridge patch in generated On() for singular Oidc sub-message until plugin updated.
- Key files: app/config.go, loginpage/loginpage.go, service/whoami.go, app/router.go, keys/resolver.go, service/discovery.go + _test.go, service/jwks.go + _test.go, service/oidcconfig.go + _test.go, proto/auth/issuer/v1/issuer.proto + gen/, frontend/src/pages/IssuerDetail.tsx, service/router.go, V2_FEDERATION.md.
- Next per plan: PKCE flow handlers + signed auth-request cookie (Phase 3 sequencing) or finish remaining minimal Phase 1 (mgr external register, more UI). Then User linked_identities + JIT, access JWT delivery, loginpage evolution, full tests/docs/mgr.

Verification gates (per phase): go test -race ./... green; manual local run (v1 paths still work: POST /login, shadow, /authz/check, /whoami, admin SPA); new federated happy path with test KIND_EXTERNAL; discovery + JWKS shapes correct; cross-origin cookies; mgr recover-admin untouched; no secrets in mgr paths.

This epic tracks the implementation. Update status via bd updates/closes. Historical narrative from initial planning sessions lives in closed issues + git history.

title: Phase 3: PKCE handlers + signed state cookie + IdP exchange
description:
Core federated login flow (the main new path):
- New oauth/ package (or service/oauth.go + helpers): pkce.go, statecookie.go, handlers.
- GET /oauth/authorize?idp=<issuer_id>&redirect_uri=...&response_type=code&... :
  - Validate idp is active KIND_EXTERNAL with OIDC config loaded.
  - Generate code_verifier + code_challenge (S256), state.
  - Build short-lived signed state-payload cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite, domain via publicsuffix eTLD+1 like shadow). Sign with KIND_SELF issuer's current key (reuse resolver.SigningKey or LiveKey; claims include verifier, redirect_uri, state, original params, exp ~5-10m).
  - Redirect to IdP authorization_endpoint (from config or discovery) with client_id, code_challenge, state, scope=openid email profile, etc.
- GET /oauth/callback?code=...&state=... :
  - Verify/parse state cookie (using resolver.VerificationKey for the kid), check exp + state match, extract verifier + original redirect_uri.
  - Clear state cookie (MaxAge=-1).
  - Load issuer OIDC config, decrypt client_secret (per-process cache like LiveKey).
  - Exchange code at IdP token_endpoint (POST, basic auth or post with client_id/secret + code_verifier).
  - Verify ID token signature (fetch IdP JWKS or use pinned jwks_uri from config; small OIDC client helper or direct).
  - Extract sub + email_at_link per claim_map on the issuer's oidc.
  - Lookup or JIT-provision User via (issuer_id, subject) + policy.
  - Mint shadow Token (via existing Token.Issue / Loginer-equivalent path) + optionally short-lived access JWT.
  - Set shadow cookie (parent domain).
  - Redirect back to original redirect_uri (with code or tokens per response_type; or return JSON if not browser redirect).
- Support multiple IdPs via ?idp=.
- Also consider /oauth/token for non-browser clients (direct code exchange) — may be later or out of initial slice.
- Endpoints registered additively in app/router.go (public, no auth).
- Requires: small http client for token exchange + JWKS fetch; PKCE challenge helper; signed cookie helper (JWT claims or custom with our signer).
State cookie issuer: prefer the default KIND_SELF (cfg.IssuerID). Short TTL makes it low risk.
This is the big orchestration slice; reuses heavily (configurator for secret, resolver for keys, Token aggregate, existing checker etc.).
acceptance_criteria: Happy path with configured test KIND_EXTERNAL: authorize redirects to IdP with challenge, callback verifies state, exchanges, verifies ID token, JITs or finds User, issues shadow (cookie set) + access JWT, redirects back. Tampering / expired state rejected. go test -race for oauth package + integration. v1 /login + shadow flows unaffected. Discovery advertises the endpoints.
notes: Per original sequencing, this was 'Phase 3' but can proceed once Phase 1 core (or remaining minimal) is solid. State cookie reuses our signing machinery — no new KeyProvider work. See root epic design for open calls around access JWT on this path, exact response shape, etc.

title: Phase 1 core completed: Issuer OIDCConfig proto + hand-written configurator + tests + minimal frontend + generator bridge
description:
Additive extension to Issuer aggregate for KIND_EXTERNAL OIDC clients (Phase 1 of V2):
- proto/auth/issuer/v1/issuer.proto: OIDCConfig message (client_id, wrapped_client_secret + key_provider/master_key_ref, discovery_url or pinned endpoints, allowed_audiences, claim_map, OIDCJITPolicy enum + jit_* fields), embed 'oidc' on Issuer (for EXTERNAL only), extend Register/Registered with initial_oidc, new SetOIDCConfig/ClearOIDCConfig commands + matching events.
- clang-format, buf generate (Go+TS), frontend TS clients updated.
- service/oidcconfig.go: NewOIDCConfigurator(issuerRepo, provider, ref) + Set (encrypts via KeyProvider.Encrypt + Apply), Clear, DecryptClientSecret, PrepareForRegister. Reuses KeyProvider exactly like keys/resolver (no plaintext in events/aggregates). Thin wrapper, panics on nil like Loginer.
- service/oidcconfig_test.go: roundtrip (Set+Load+Decrypt+Clear via memory repo + local provider); prepare path.
- Minimal frontend: IssuerDetail.tsx shows client ID, 'configured' badge for wrapped secret, endpoints, JIT policy (write-only secret; no create form yet).
- Temporary bridge in generated issuer.protosource.pb.go On() to assign aggregate.Oidc = e.GetConfig() (and nil on clear) because protoc-gen-protosource did not emit singular sub-message copies for events at the time (collections via GetGrant worked; generator enhancement needed later).
No change to bootstrap/RegisterDefaultIssuer (still SELF only). mgr/frontend full create forms deferred.
All tests/builds green post-changes.

title: Update protosource dep to v0.7.1 + adopt by-name singular embed convention (GH#96/PR#97)
description: Upstream PR #97 (issue #96) changes singular embedded message events to match aggregate fields by NAME (reverting the experimental by-type inference). v0.7.1 generator hard-fails when an event carries an embedded message present on the aggregate under a different field name. Rename Issuer OIDC embed fields (initial_oidc/config -> oidc) on commands+events to match aggregate field 'oidc'; add oidc field to OIDCConfigCleared for by-name clear-to-nil. Update go.mod, regenerate, fix hand-written refs.

title: Upstream generator fix needed for singular embedded messages on aggregates (OIDCConfigSet etc.)
description:
The protoc-gen-protosource generator lacks support for singular (non-collection) embedded message fields on aggregates in the event On() applicator.

See the detailed upstream issue for full explanation, reproduction, code pointers into the generator (protosource.gotext template + protosourceify.go collection vs. regular event paths), and acceptance criteria:

https://github.com/funinthecloud/protosource/issues/96

This is the root cause of the 'we had to patch generated files' problem that surfaced in the OIDCConfig (Phase 1) work and the CI test failures after buf generate.

Once the generator is enhanced, we can:
- Remove the manual patches from gen/ in this repo
- Re-run clean buf generate + make gen
- Stop the 'temporary bridge' workaround

Related local files: proto/auth/issuer/v1/issuer.proto (the oidc field + Set/Clear events), service/oidcconfig.go + _test.go (the code that relies on GetOidc() after Apply), the previous manual edits that were in issuer.protosource.pb.go and issuermgr/main.go.

Track progress via the GitHub issue; we can do the generator work in a dedicated session on the protosource checkout.

title: Access JWT delivery + authorizer evolution (short identity JWT alongside shadow)
description:
On successful federated callback (and optionally evolve /login response):
- Return short-lived access JWT (different TTL e.g. 5-15m, different aud/claims/scope/azp, signed by our key) in addition to minting the long shadow Token.
- Response evolution: include access_token, (id_token?), expires_in, plus set shadow cookie. (May affect LoginResponseJSON too for consistency/break-glass.)
- Persistence: access JWTs are largely fire-and-forget (short TTL for revocation window); Token aggregate remains the source for shadow + full session (instant revoke via revoke). Design may add ephemeral storage or just issue on the fly.
- httpauthz / directauthz evolution: prefer Bearer access token for identity-only needs (verify locally via our JWKS if possible, no /authz/check hop); still require full /authz/check + shadow for function-grant protected calls. Pluggable? New mode or TokenSource options.
- Downstream impact: document for consumers (e.g. todoapp etc.).
- Revocation story: short access = time-bound; shadow for immediate.
Keep /authz/check as the authoritative function gate.
See root epic open design calls (claims differences, persistence decision).
acceptance_criteria: Callback (and optionally /login) responses include access_token with short exp; authorizers can optionally accept+verify fresh access JWT for identity enrichment without calling check; shadow still required for full authz; tests cover both paths; docs updated.
notes: This can be done in parallel with or right after initial PKCE happy path (the callback already has the user context to mint both). Requires the JWKS work already landed.

title: Phase 2: User LinkedIdentity + JIT provisioning
description:
Extend User aggregate for federated identities (1 User : N linked):
- Proto: message LinkedIdentity { issuer_id, subject, email_at_link, linked_at }; map<string, LinkedIdentity> linked_identities on User (key '{issuer_id}:{subject}').
- Collection events: IdentityLinked, IdentityUnlinked (ADD/REMOVE style like RoleGrant).
- Commands: LinkIdentity / UnlinkIdentity (admin/manual) or initially internal to oauth callback.
- Relax User Create: password_hash optional (or new CreateFederated command). Existing local users keep hash.
- Directory: extend or new FindByLinkedIdentity for fast callback path (before full user load). For Dynamo: GSI or query pattern.
- JIT in oauth callback (after successful IdP exchange + sub/email extract per claim_map):
  - Load issuer, check oidc.jit_policy (REJECT / AUTO / DOMAIN_RULE).
  - REJECT: error.
  - AUTO: create User (no password_hash) + link identity + optional default role.
  - DOMAIN_RULE: if email domain matches configured, grant specific role_id.
- Update Loginer? No — keep pure for break-glass. New thin federated mint path or reuse Token.Issue after user resolved.
- UI: whoami / admin UserDetail may surface linked identities (privacy note: primary email?).
- Tests: multi-link same user from different IdPs, JIT create, domain rule grant, reject case.
Note on UserDirectory: currently FindByEmail; federated primary path will key on (issuer,subject).
Depends on Phase 1 OIDCConfig (to have the policy + claim_map on the issuer).
acceptance_criteria: User proto has linked_identities map + events; Create allows no password_hash for federated; JIT logic in callback respects per-issuer policy and creates/links correctly; directory lookup by linked identity works; go test -race + manual flows pass; v1 local Create + password users unaffected.
notes: See V2_FEDERATION.md for LinkedIdentity shape and rationale (Google sub stable, email can change; email_at_link is display only). This is aggregate + orchestration work (mostly in oauth handler + thin service).

title: Mgr CLI: external issuer registration command (with secret handling)
description:
Operational support (can be done with remaining Phase 1 or later):

This complements the frontend forms (miy.3) and is useful for CI/bootstrap before UI is ready.
acceptance_criteria: (or equivalent) succeeds, creates KIND_EXTERNAL + OIDCConfig with wrapped secret (verifiable via configurator decrypt in a service process); secret never appears in command output or logs; works in environments without master key; documented in mgr help / README.
notes: mgr commands are the 'direct' path that work even if HTTP service is down. See cmd/protosource-authmgr/ and existing bootstrap/recover-admin/diagnose. (Fixed from initial creation that had shell quoting issues in the command.)
